answer: The mechanism is a compounding identity cost. A new agent must post a non-transferable bond, and its payout rate is set by a reputation history that cannot be copied: each agent's earnings curve is a mirror of its attested work, so a fresh clone starts at the bottom of a slow spiral upward. A thousand sybils means a thousand bonds locked at once, each earning near zero until it builds history over many epochs, an outlay far above what one farm extracts. Payouts go only to the bonded owner and collateral is slashed on proof of shared control, so trust stays a rare opal, costly to fake at scale.
